From: security@primuscloud.com

Subject: Tenant boundary questions for S3-managed backups and SOC 2 linkage

Hi Aditya,

We are reviewing Redwoods' controls for our upcoming vendor risk assessment. A couple items we need clarified to close our SOC 2 linkage:

1) For customer backups that you store in S3 (region: us-west-2), is that storage in a shared bucket or per-tenant buckets?
2) Does Redwood rely on the cloud provider SOC 2 report for encryption-at-rest controls for backups, or do you treat it as a subservice carve-out? If the latter, can you confirm the carve-out boundary and provide the provider's SOC report and a bridge letter if available?
3) Please provide a short inventory (or link) of subprocessors that have access to backups or key material (KMS).
4) Audit period question: our assessment covers 2026-10-01 through 2027-03-31. Can you confirm whether Redwood's most recent Type II report covers that period or if we should accept a bridge letter?

If you can share the SOC 2 report and a bridge letter or summary by EOD Monday that would be ideal.

Thanks,
Security Team

Thanks Aditya — a couple follow-ups to help our intake team:

• "Per-tenant prefixes" is helpful. Can you confirm whether tenant data can be accessed by other tenants in practice (shared ACLs, cross-tenant role policies, etc.) or if you enforce IAM + bucket policies at tenant level?
• KMS: do you use a customer-managed key (CMK) for any customers, or only provider-managed keys? If CMKs are supported, which subprocessors (if any) have administrative access to the CMK?
• For the provider SOC report: do you consider the cloud provider controls in-scope (i.e., you rely on their SOC 2 for certain control objectives), or do you treat them as carved out and provide your own evidence?

If you can provide the provider SOC2 PDF, Redwood's Type II PDF, and a short bridge-letter draft that maps which controls are covered by the provider report, that would address most of our review.

Appreciate it — timeline: we are targeting final vendor approval by 2027-06-18.

Hi Maria / Primus security team — thanks for the patience. Notes below and attachments included.

Quick answers up-front:
- Tenant isolation: we enforce tenant-level IAM roles and S3 prefix policies. No cross-tenant ACLs are used and platform services are scoped to tenant IDs; in practice, other tenants cannot list or access another tenant's prefixes.
- KMS: Redwood supports provider-managed KMS keys for all customers by default. We also offer customer-managed keys (CMKs) for enterprise customers under Dedicated/Private deployments only; when CMKs are used, customers manage keys in their account and Redwood does not have administrative access.
- Provider SOC2: We consider the cloud provider SOC 2 as a subservice report for certain infrastructure controls (physical security, underlying hypervisor, network fabric). Redwood's SOC 2 Type II maps provider controls where applicable; we treat some provider responsibilities as covered by the provider report and provide a bridge letter that maps provider control IDs to Redwood control procedures.

Attachments (attached to this thread):
- Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_2026.pdf (pdf, 3.2MB) — Redwood's latest Type II report covering 2026-04-01 through 2027-03-31.
- bridge-letter-draft.docx (docx, 45KB) — draft bridge letter that maps cloud provider controls to Redwood controls; includes an explicit carve-out description for the cloud provider's management of physical infrastructure and KMS key lifecycle.
- subprocessor_inventory_2027-06.csv (csv, 12KB) — inventory of subprocessors; column includes "access_type" where KMS_admin is flagged where applicable.

Relevant notes and redlines:
• Audit period: Redwood's Type II covers 2026-04-01 to 2027-03-31, which is slightly outside your requested window (2026-10-01 to 2027-03-31). The Type II covers the latter part of your window fully. We can provide the bridge-letter to explicitly state coverage for control objectives during the overlapping period (2026-10-01 to 2027-03-31).

• KMS admin access: per the attached subprocessor inventory, the cloud provider (listed) has KMS_admin flagged for provider-managed keys. Redwood employees do not have KMS_admin on provider-managed keys; access to decrypted payloads is restricted by platform service layers and audited. For Dedicated/Private customers using CMKs, the customer holds the key admin roles.

• Tenant separation evidence: for your convenience we included a short excerpt in the bridge letter describing the S3 prefix policy enforcement and an example IAM policy. If you need logs showing per-tenant access events for a given date range we can supply a scoped export under an NDA.

Next steps:
1) Please confirm you received the three attachments (we can also upload to a secure portal if preferred).
2) Let us know if you need any redlines to the bridge letter; Rishi and I can coordinate a quick review cycle.

Regards,
Lauren Bishop

• We will accept the Type II that covers 2026-04-01 to 2027-03-31 for our window; please add the clause in the bridge letter explicitly stating overlap with our requested period (2026-10-01 to 2027-03-31).

If you can update the bridge letter with the overlap clause and the answer on CMK automation by COB Monday we'll be in a position to close.
